sections.html:
Cabot is the largest city in Lonoke County and part of the Little Rock-North Little Rock-Conway metro area. Its population rose from 1,321 in 1960 to 8,319 in 1990, 15,261 in 2000, 23,776 in 2010 and 26,569 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 27,711. The 2020 count showed 10,637 housing units, with 6.3 percent vacant.

Interstate 57 and U.S. 67 and 167 form a four-lane freeway on the northwest side of the city that leads about 22 miles southwest to Little Rock. Jacksonville is 9 miles away on the same route. Many residents commute to Little Rock, and about 40 percent of Little Rock Air Force Base's military personnel are reported to live in Cabot. That gives the city two steady groups of buyers.

sections.h2: Selling to military and commuter buyers
sections.html:
• A seller with orders or a job transfer may care more about a firm closing date than a long listing period.
  • Distance to the freeway and to Jacksonville or Little Rock is worth stating up front.
  • Buyers who commute will ask how far the house is from the on-ramp.

The school district holds a Purple Star designation for supporting military families, which families moving to the base notice.

Cabot has hot, humid summers and mild to cool winters, with about 53 inches of precipitation over roughly 92 days a year. A tornado on March 29, 1976 killed five people and destroyed several buildings, and City Plaza was built on the rebuilt site. Severe weather is part of life here.

  • Roof age, shingle condition and prior storm claims.
  • Windows, doors and garage doors that have taken wind damage.
  • Moisture in attics, crawl spaces and slabs after wet seasons.
  • Cooling system age.

Damage you have not repaired does not have to hold up a sale. A buyer who purchases as is will price the work instead of asking you to finish it.

Cabot Public Schools serve Cabot, Austin and Ward, plus most of northern Lonoke County. The district includes Cabot High School and Cabot Junior High School North. Because it reaches beyond city limits, a mailing address that says Cabot does not always mean the same district boundary. Check the school assignment for your parcel before you list.

sections.h2: Permits and the Planning and Zoning office
sections.html:
Cabot's Planning and Zoning department at 1 City Plaza, Suite A handles residential permits and the zoning map. Permits are listed for additions and remodels, decks, electrical, plumbing and mechanical work, swimming pools, water heater replacement, generators, roofs, solar panels, sprinkler systems, storage buildings, sun rooms, porch enclosures and retaining walls.

Homeowners may do many repairs themselves but still need permits and must follow code. Contractors should have purchased the permit for the work, and the work requires one or more inspections depending on the job. Planning and Zoning can be reached at 501-843-4819, and the city's GIS map has a zoning layer worth checking before you apply for a planning permit.

Before listing, look back at any work done on the house: a new roof, a deck, a water heater or an accessory building. If a permit was never pulled, ask the department what to do. A cash buyer will usually take a house that way, though you should tell them what you know.

Arkansas real property tax is due between the first business day of March and October 15 of the year after the levy, and the collector adds a 10 percent penalty to balances left after October 15. Cabot properties are billed through the Lonoke County collector. Because tax is paid in arrears, the person who owns the house on the assessment date is billed for the year, and the closing statement decides how the amount is split between buyer and seller.

sections.h2: Gathering what a buyer will ask for
sections.html:
Start with the paperwork you can find quickly: the deed, your last tax statement, receipts for a roof or water heater and any permit that was pulled. Then add the facts a buyer cannot see from the street, such as when the cooling system was replaced and whether the roof has had a storm claim.

A buyer who commutes to Little Rock or to the base wants the same few answers. How long is the drive to the on-ramp, which school assignment applies and what do the utilities cost. Write the answers down once and reuse them with every buyer who calls.

Heirs or out-of-town owners can usually do all of this from home. The county record and the city office answer by phone, and the title company handles the rest.

• Was a permit issued for the roof, water heater, deck or accessory building?
  • Does the zoning map show anything unusual on my lot?
  • Is any inspection still open?
  • Who should I call if the original contractor did not purchase the permit?

Ask these before you list, not after a buyer finds the gap. A department that tells you a permit is missing early gives you time to decide how to handle it.

Arkansas charges a real property transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of the consideration on transfers above $100. Ask the title company to show it on the settlement statement along with the tax line and recording fees.

The county beyond town is rural. Lonoke County moved from cotton to rice after a 1904 demonstration, and rice farming remains part of its economy. Acreage and country houses outside the city limits can raise different questions than a subdivision lot inside Cabot, so tell a buyer exactly where your parcel lies.

Sellers here often have a house that needs updating, a job transfer, a rental with tenants, or an inherited house with several owners. The Air Force Base link means some owners have only weeks to move.

Compare a listing with a cash sale on timing, repair costs and what you keep in the end. Cabot has its own zoning code, so confirm anything that affects your house with city staff.

After you accept an offer, the title company searches the county record for unpaid tax and recorded liens. Bring your last tax statement, deed and any permit paperwork. If you are on orders, tell the buyer your required date early.

At closing you sign the deed, and the tax balance and any lien are paid from your proceeds. A cash sale with a clean search can close on a date you set.

faqs.q: What county is Cabot, Arkansas in?
faqs.a: Cabot is in Lonoke County, and it is the county's largest city. The county seat is the city of Lonoke.

faqs.q: How far is Cabot from Little Rock?
faqs.a: About 22 miles southwest on the I-57 and U.S. 67 and 167 freeway. Jacksonville is 9 miles from Cabot on the same route.

faqs.q: When are Arkansas property taxes due for a Cabot house?
faqs.a: By October 15, with a 10 percent penalty on unpaid balances after that date. Collection starts the first business day of March, and installments are allowed under state law.

faqs.q: Do I need permits for repairs on my Cabot house?
faqs.a: Yes for many jobs. Cabot lists permits for roofs, water heaters, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, decks, pools, generators and similar work. Call Planning and Zoning at 501-843-4819 if you are not sure.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Cabot house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell as-is to a cash buyer, who will account for repairs in the price. Tell the buyer about any known problems.
